_comment: The `backends` block of config.json — merge it into your node's config, do not use this file directly.
It is what makes a node serve the LLM API at /v1 and appear on the site's Models page. Without it the node
has no /v1 surface at all, `/api/models` answers an empty list, and the page says so rather than pretending.
Declared, not probed: the node advertises what an operator configured rather than whatever container happens
to be running. `upstream` is the model server's own address — internal on every real deployment, and never
`models` is what a caller passes as `model`. It must match what the backend serves under that name; for vLLM
`concurrency` is how many requests a backend runs at once. The language model's is 1 because it sits behind
the shared runtime lease; transcription and image run on their own GPUs and set their own.
The three scripts in this directory bring these up: serve-llm.sh, serve-stt.sh, serve-image.sh. Each takes
MODEL_DIR, SERVED_MODEL_NAME, PORT and GPUS from the environment, and DETACH=1 leaves it running.
AS OF 2026-09-25 the production node has no backends block: it answers every other route and serves
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, but publishes no model list. Applying this is a decision for whoever runs it — the site
renders that state honestly in the meantime.
